ch28.d.particle: Kind of particle launched (mass and charge)
ch28.d.B: Magnitude $B$ of the uniform field into the page; takes effect at once while running
ch28.d.compare: Launch three particles at 1, 2 and 3 × 10⁶ m/s together
ch28.d.v: Launch speed $v$ (one particle when speed comparison is off)
ch28.l.goal.perp: The magnetic force $\vec F = q\vec v \times \vec B$ is always perpendicular to the velocity: it does no work, the speed stays constant and the path is a circle
ch28.l.goal.T: The radius $r = mv/\lvert q\rvert B$ grows with speed; the period $T = 2\pi m/\lvert q\rvert B$ does not depend on speed
ch28.l.obs.perp: $\vec F$ (purple) is always perpendicular to $\vec v$ (vermilion) and points to the centre
ch28.l.obs.r: Speed comparison: faster particles move on larger circles
ch28.l.obs.T: Speed comparison: all three particles return to the start together, so the period does not depend on speed
ch28.l.obs.sign: Protons and alpha particles circle counter-clockwise, electrons clockwise (sign of the charge)
ch28.l.obs.B: Double $B$ while running: the readouts $r$ and $T$ halve, and the circles shrink
ch28.l.assume: Uniform field in vacuum; gravity and radiation neglected; non-relativistic speeds (at most $0.01c$). Time runs slowed down, in ns
ch28.c.d.ratio: Frequency $f$ of the gap voltage as a multiple of the cyclotron frequency $f_c$
ch28.c.d.V0: Peak $V_0$ of the alternating voltage between the dees
ch28.c.goal.res: The cyclotron frequency $f_c = \lvert q\rvert B/2\pi m$ does not depend on speed, so a fixed-frequency voltage can accelerate the particle again and again
ch28.c.goal.K: Each gap crossing adds $qV$ of kinetic energy; the radius grows and the path is a spiral
ch28.c.obs.step: $K(t)$ climbs in steps, one per half turn, each when the gap voltage peaks
ch28.c.obs.spiral: Inside a dee the proton moves on a half circle; the time for a half circle does not depend on the radius
ch28.c.obs.detune: $f \neq f_c$: the phase at each crossing drifts, acceleration turns into deceleration, the spiral winds back in and the energy stays far below the in-tune value
ch28.c.obs.V0: A larger gap voltage gives taller steps and fewer turns; the exit energy is the same, $K_\text{max} = (qBR)^2/2m$ = 120 keV
ch28.c.assume: Proton, $B$ = 1 T, dee radius $R$ = 5 cm, gap 6 mm (drawn wider than in real machines), gap voltage set high to keep the number of turns small; the magnet pole is a little wider than the dees; when the orbit radius reaches $R$ a deflector extracts the proton (straight line afterwards); fringe fields neglected; non-relativistic
